dehydrated_text:
So that's the second thing we know: the Romans crucified Jesus, although we don't know why. We also know they killed him by nailing him to a wooden cross, an awful way to die because you suffocate slowly over about three days.

The Romans used crucifixion for two types of people: thieves and bandits, considered the lowest, and rebels trying to overthrow Roman rule. Jesus was likely seen as a rebel or was considered one by the Romans.

A brother named James the Just inherited Jesus' movement after his death; this movement was called the poor or Ibionites.

Now, according to the Bible, there are at least four different biographies of Jesus: Mark, Matthew, Luke, and John. The main story is that Jesus is the son of God sent to redeem humanity's sins by sacrificing himself as a scapegoat on Earth.

At this time, in Judea (Roman province), Jesus preached healing, cleansing from demons, and spreading the gospel against the teachings of Jewish priests who emphasized strict adherence to laws and traditions. The Jewish priests plotted against him, leading to his betrayal by Judas Iscariot, trial by Pontius Pilate, crucifixion, death, resurrection after three days, and subsequent appearances to disciples.

He told them he would return and that they should spread the gospel until his eventual return.
